title: 教育与社会阅读词汇
goal: 辨认教育与社会词汇，理解群体比较及其限制。

points.label: 辨认教育与社会领域词汇
理解群体比较及其限制条件

sources.title: 全国大学英语四、六级考试大纲
sources.used: 阅读课程内容与材料形式

body.p: 教育与社会类文章常比较资源、机会和不同群体的结果。平均值说明两组的整体差异，组里每个人的情况可以不同。

body.box: On average, participants in one group traveled farther. Some participants in the other group also traveled a long way.

body.p: on average 表示这是两组的整体比较。另一组中也有人走得很远。

body.box:
A district allocates funding for school libraries using the number of enrolled students. A review found that larger schools therefore received more money in total. The review also compared funding per student, which answered a different question: how much was available for each enrolled student rather than for each school. A large total alone did not establish that students at a large school received more resources individually.

The reviewers also examined travel to public libraries. On average, students in outlying areas traveled farther than students near the town center. However, some students near the center also lived far from a public library. The average described a difference between groups, not the journey of each student.

The district considered adding a mobile library stop in outlying areas. Before deciding, officials wanted to know the number of students who could reach each proposed stop and the cost of operating it. The review provided a starting point for that decision, but further information about individual access was needed.

body.p: 第一段区分两个数字：学校拿到的资金总额和每名学生分到的资金。大学校的总额高，比较学生个人的资源要看人均金额。
第二段的 on average 表示这是群体之间的比较。第三段决定是否增设流动图书馆站点，依据是能到达站点的学生人数和运行成本。

groups.fill: A college offers a course at two locations. The cou{rse} is off{ered} on diff{erent} days s{o} that stud{ents} can cho{ose} the loca{tion} and ti{me} that su{it} their sche{dules}. The college records attendance at each location. It also asks enrolled students about travel time and work commitments. These answers can help staff understand which schedules are useful to current students. They do not show why people who have not enrolled stay away. A broader review would need information from those people as well.
notes: offered：被动结构说明课程开设。
choose：后面列出可选的地点和时间。
schedules：their schedules 指学生的日程。

groups.text:
A district examined access to adult training at two community centers. One center offered courses in the morning, while the other offered evening courses. The district asked enrolled participants how long they traveled to attend. On average, participants at the evening center reported longer journeys. The finding described the two groups as a whole; some morning participants also traveled a long way.

The survey included only people already attending a course. It could not show whether potential participants avoided a center because of travel time, work schedules or other reasons. Staff therefore proposed a second survey that would include residents who had not enrolled. They also wanted to compare public transport schedules near both centers.

A proposal to add an evening course at the morning center might reduce travel for some residents, but its effect would depend on demand and staffing. The district planned to estimate the number of interested residents and the cost of hiring an instructor. It would then evaluate the proposal using both access and cost, rather than assuming that one group's average journey applied to every individual.

items.stem: What did the first survey measure?
options: Travel time reported by enrolled participants
The cost of hiring an evening instructor
Reasons all residents avoided the centers
Public transport schedules near both centers
items.why: asked enrolled participants how long they traveled 说明调查内容。

items.stem: What does the average comparison establish?
options: Every evening participant traveled farther than every morning participant.
The evening group reported a longer journey on average.
No morning participant traveled far to reach a course.
All residents preferred the evening center to the morning center.
items.why: On average ... evening center reported longer journeys 说明群体平均差异。

options: To compare bus schedules near both centers
To compare only people already taking courses
To include residents not represented in the first survey
To ask morning participants about their journeys
items.why: second survey ... include residents who had not enrolled 补充未报名者的信息。

items.stem: What does enrolled mean in the first paragraph?
options: Hired as course instructors
Surveyed about public transport
Excluded from evening courses
Registered to take a course
items.why: people already attending a course 对应已注册参加课程的人。

items.stem: What would the district consider when evaluating the new course?
options: Interest and the cost of an instructor
Only the morning group's longest journey
Only the number of existing instructors
Transport schedules without residents' interest
items.why: estimate the number of interested residents and the cost of hiring an instructor 指出两项依据。

groups.fill: A town reviewed the use of a public hall. The rev{iew} compared atten{dance} at diff{erent} events a{nd} asked visi{tors} about th{eir} travel ti{me} to t{he} building. T{he} results sho{wed} variation among visitors. Some people walked from nearby streets, while others used buses. The study included those attending events, not residents who stayed away. Staff will use the findings to plan another survey. That survey will ask a broader group about possible changes to opening hours.

groups.text:
A town studied access to a public sports center after a change in its bus routes. Researchers asked center members how they traveled there and how long their journeys took. Members living in the northern district reported longer journeys on average than members living in the southern district. Some southern members nevertheless reported long journeys, and some northern members reported short ones.

The researchers emphasized that their sample consisted of current members. People who had stopped visiting or never joined were absent from the survey. The findings could describe journeys among respondents but could not establish why other residents did not use the center. A follow-up study would ask a wider group about travel, fees and schedules.

One proposal would add a bus stop closer to the center. Supporters argued that a shorter walk from the bus could improve access for some residents. The town would need the transport operator's agreement and an estimate of the cost. The survey offered a reason to investigate access, but the average journey alone did not demonstrate how many additional residents would use the center if the stop were added.

options: Bus routes used before and after the change
Journey times reported by members in two districts
Reasons residents in two districts stopped visiting
Walking distances from a proposed bus stop
items.why: northern district reported longer journeys on average than ... southern district 指出比较对象。

items.stem: What follows from the reported averages?
options: Every northern member had a longer journey than every southern member.
No southern member had a long journey to the center.
The groups differed on average, though journeys varied within each.
Northern residents used the center less than southern ones.
items.why: 原文先说北区会员 on average 路程更长，又说 Some southern members nevertheless reported long journeys。第三项同时保留了平均差异和组内差异。

items.stem: What does sample refer to in the second paragraph?
options: The group of current members surveyed
Every resident living in the town
People who had stopped visiting the center
The residents asked in the follow-up study
items.why: sample consisted of current members 说明样本是受调查的现有会员。

items.stem: Why would the follow-up study ask a wider group?
options: To repeat the questions for current members
To omit all current members from the study
To estimate the cost of the new bus stop
To include people the first survey missed
items.why: 原文说 People who had stopped visiting or never joined were absent from the survey，后续调查要补上这些人，即第四项。

items.stem: What condition must be met for the proposed bus stop?
options: The survey must show more residents will come.
The transport operator must agree to the change.
The sports center must remove its membership fee.
Current members must agree to the new stop.
items.why: would need the transport operator's agreement 指出实施条件。
